# Implement the work

Load when a request involves any of these terms: implement, edit, files changed, learning notes.

## Step instructions

Follow the current run's dispatch directive, if one is rendered.

Make the change at the WorkNode's target so its expected_post_state holds. Stay
strictly scoped to it — no unrelated files, no /graph. Keep the edit minimal and
aligned to the description, then run the narrow tests for what you changed.
Record every file you created or modified as fact files_changed — required.

Record fact learning_notes: 1-3 sentences naming the non-obvious decision, tradeoff
or assumption behind the shape you chose — not a restatement of changes_summary, and
not a list of the files. Optional and non-gating: it never blocks implement → verify.

Record fact dispatch_model: the model that performed THIS attempt (your own model
id, whether you're a dispatched sub-agent or the orchestrator working inline).
Optional and non-gating -- the escalation ladder uses it, when present, to look up
what comes next.

## Facts

- `changes_implemented`: Whether the change was made at the WorkNode's target.
- `changes_summary`: What you actually did and why, in prose -- the account beside the verdict, mirroring verify's acceptance_evidence and review's review_findings. EITHER this or changes_implemented opens the step; supplying both is fine and neither is required when the other is present, so an agent with nothing to add is never forced to invent it. Persisted on the WorkNode in the generic StepEvidence record when the step is left.
- `files_changed`: Every file path you created or modified for this change.
- `learning_notes`: 1-3 sentences of why-this-shape rationale — the non-obvious decision, tradeoff or assumption behind the change, not a restatement of changes_summary. Optional and NON-GATING, so implement never waits on it to reach verify. Persisted in the generic StepEvidence record when supplied.
- `dispatch_model`: The rung position (index in the escalation ladder) that performed THIS attempt. Optional and NON-GATING. Read live by escalation_handoff_predicate (subagent_handoff.yaml) via list_at_offset against settings.models[<provider>].list -- no separate derived fact; a once-derived value would go stale the moment a LATER attempt records its own dispatch_model, letting a stale rung compare against orchestrator_model instead of the real one.
